basic_details.job_title: Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026 Notification Out - Apply Online for 250 Posts
basic_details.short_information: The Supreme Court of India invites online applications from Indian citizens who fulfil the prescribed qualifications and eligibility conditions, as on 1st September 2026, for selection of suitable candidates for preparation of a panel for filling up 250 tentative vacancies of Junior Court Assistant. The number of posts may be subject to change due to administrative exigencies and/or the requirement of the Registry. Register for Job Alerts

application_fee.details: Eligible candidates are required to apply online for which a link will be provided through the website of the Supreme Court of India, www.sci.gov.in. The application will be accepted through online registration only; no postal application form shall be accepted. | Fee must be paid through online mode only, via the payment gateway provided by UCO Bank. Fee shall not be accepted in any other form, and once paid, will not be refunded under any circumstances or in any eventuality.

age_limit.details: As on 1st September 2026, candidates should not be below 18 years of age. The upper age limit for candidates is 30 years. | Usual age relaxation is admissible to candidates belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes (Non-Creamy Layer), Physically Challenged, and Ex-Servicemen, as per Government of India Rules. Relaxation up to a maximum of 5 years, over and above the prescribed age limit of 30 years, is admissible to dependents of freedom fighters. No relaxation in age will be allowed to candidates working in other Government Departments/Public Sector Undertakings/Nationalized Banks, etc.

In case a large number of candidates qualify the Objective Type Test by securing the minimum qualifying 50 marks or more
candidates will be shortlisted for the second stage (Typing Speed Test and Written Test) in the ratio of 1:10 against the number of tentative vacancies
based on the merit list.
The Written Test (Descriptive) answer sheets will be evaluated only for candidates who successfully qualify the Typing Speed Test
since qualifying the Typing Speed Test is mandatory. Candidates who successfully qualify all three tests — Objective Type Test
Typing Speed Test
and Written Test — will be shortlisted for Interview in the ratio of 1:3 against the number of tentative vacancies.
Candidates will have to exercise their option to select cities in order of preference. The Registry reserves the right to shift test centre(s) and/or increase or decrease the number of test centre(s)
keeping in view the number of application forms received. No request for change of City/Test centre and/or date(s) of Tests/Interview will be entertained.

within the notified objection window
on payment of a fee of Rs. 100/- per objection
which will be refunded if the objection is found valid.
how_to_apply: SCI Junior Court Assistant Apply Online process is entirely online, through the link provided on the Supreme Court of India's website.
Visit the official website: www.sci.gov.in and access the online application link provided for the recruitment.

Fill in the online Application Form with accurate personal, educational, and category details. Note that Name, Father's name, Mother's name, and Date of Birth must be entered exactly as per the High School Certificate/Xth Board Examination certificate.

Upload scanned copies of your recent photograph, signature, and requisite documents (Class Xth, Class XIIth, and Graduation Certificates, caste/community certificate for reserved category candidates, and disability certificate, if applicable).
Furnish the required Undertaking confirming that you have read and understood the terms and conditions of the advertisement and will abide by them.
Make payment of the applicable application fee online, through the payment gateway provided by UCO Bank.
Preview the Application Form after successful completion, and take a printout of the filled-up form for your records (this printout need not be sent to the Registry).
Submit the application on or before 28th October 2026, till 11:55 p.m.
Retain your Application Number carefully, for generation of the Admit Card from the link to be provided on the Supreme Court of India website.
important_instructions: Admission at all stages of the Examination — Objective Type Test, Typing Speed Test, Written Test (Descriptive), and Interview — will be purely provisional; eligibility documents will be checked/verified at the time of document verification. If a candidate is found guilty of impersonation, submitting fabricated/false documents, or furnishing false information at any stage, they will be removed/disqualified, prosecuted, and debarred from future appointment in the Registry. Application once submitted cannot be withdrawn or modified; candidates should ensure all particulars are correct before final submission. Fee once paid will not be refunded under any circumstances or in any eventuality. In case a candidate submits more than one Application Form, only the form with the latest Application Number, lastly submitted, will be considered; no correspondence requesting acceptance of previous forms will be entertained. No request for change of category filled in the online Application Form will be entertained. Candidates must have a valid personal e-mail ID and mobile number, kept active throughout the recruitment process, as information will be sent via SMS and e-mail. No TA/DA will be payable for appearing in the Tests/Interview. No Admit Cards will be sent by post; candidates must download them from the Supreme Court of India website. Concessions/facilities in the Tests will be extended to Persons with Disabilities as per the Government of India's prescribed Office Memorandum; the facility of a scribe may be availed by PwBD candidates by submitting the proforma at Annexure-I or Annexure-IA, along with the requisite certificate. The scribe's qualification must be a minimum of two academic years below and a maximum of three academic years below the minimum qualification for the post. Candidates working in Central/State Government Departments/Nationalized Banks/Public Sector Undertakings, etc., must submit a 'No Objection Certificate' from their employer at the time of document verification. If a candidate who was unemployed at the time of application gets employment during or after the examination process, they must immediately intimate this to the Branch Officer, Recruitment Cell, at [email protected], failing which adverse inference will be drawn by the Registry. Application forms which do not comply with the instructions shall be summarily rejected. In case of any dispute(s), the jurisdiction will be Delhi.

content_sections.text: As on 1st September 2026, candidates should not be below 18 years of age. The upper age limit for candidates is 30 years . Relaxation up to a maximum of 5 years, over and above the prescribed age limit of 30 years, is admissible to dependents of freedom fighters. There is no upper age limit for Departmental candidates of the Registry of the Supreme Court of India. No relaxation in age will be allowed to candidates working in other Government Departments/Public Sector Undertakings/Nationalized Banks, etc.

content_sections.heading: SCI Junior Court Assistant Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Eligible candidates are required to appear in the following stages of examination for selection to the post of Junior Court Assistant. In case a large number of candidates qualify the Objective Type Test by securing the minimum qualifying 50 marks or more, candidates will be shortlisted for the second stage (Typing Speed Test and Written Test) in the ratio of 1:10 against the number of tentative vacancies, based on the merit list. The Written Test (Descriptive) answer sheets will be evaluated only for candidates who successfully qualify the Typing Speed Test, since qualifying the Typing Speed Test is mandatory. Candidates who successfully qualify all three tests — Objective Type Test, Typing Speed Test, and Written Test — will be shortlisted for Interview in the ratio of 1:3 against the number of tentative vacancies. Candidates will have to exercise their option to select cities in order of preference. The Registry reserves the right to shift test centre(s) and/or increase or decrease the number of test centre(s), keeping in view the number of application forms received. No request for change of City/Test centre and/or date(s) of Tests/Interview will be entertained. There will be negative marking of 0.25 marks for each incorrect answer in the Objective Type Test (Multiple Choice Questions). Candidates may submit objections to the Answer Keys through online mode only, within the notified objection window, on payment of a fee of Rs. 100/- per objection, which will be refunded if the objection is found valid.

Candidates must have a valid personal e-mail ID and mobile number, kept active throughout the recruitment process, as information will be sent via SMS and e-mail. faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are available in Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The Supreme Court of India has announced 250 tentative vacancies for the post of Junior Court Assistant (Group-B Non-Gazetted).

faq.question: Q2. What is the qualification for Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates must have a Bachelor's degree from a recognized University in India, knowledge of computer operation, and a typing speed of 35 words per minute on computer.

faq.question: Q3. What is the age limit for Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates must be 18 to 30 years old as on 01 September 2026. Age relaxation is applicable to eligible categories as mentioned in the official notification.

faq.question: Q4. What is the salary of a Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant?
faq.answer: The Junior Court Assistant post is placed in Level 6 of the Pay Matrix, with an initial Basic Pay of Rs. 35,400 per month plus applicable allowances.

faq.question: Q5. When will online applications start for Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The online application process will start on 07 October 2026 through the official Supreme Court of India website.

faq.question: Q6. What is the last date to apply for Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The last date to submit the online application is 28 October 2026 up to 11:55 PM.

faq.question: Q7. What is the application fee for Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The application fee is Rs. 1,500 plus bank charges for General/Unreserved candidates and Rs. 750 plus bank charges for SC, ST, OBC-NCL, Ex-Servicemen and Physically Challenged candidates.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The selection process consists of an Objective Type Test, Typing Speed Test on Computer, Written Test (Descriptive) in English and Interview. Candidates must qualify in the prescribed stages.

faq.question: Q9. When will the Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Exam 2026 be held?
faq.answer: The Objective Type Test is tentatively scheduled for 20 November 2026. Dates for the Typing Speed Test, Descriptive Written Test and Interview will be announced separately.

faq.question: Q10. How can I apply online for Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Eligible candidates can apply online through the official Supreme Court of India website at www.sci.gov.in from 07 October to 28 October 2026. Candidates should complete registration, upload the required documents, pay the application fee and submit the form before the deadline.
